hypothesis: A registered concern weighting over a finite task family does real work in choosing among bag's five representing screens: distinct concerns force distinct screens (four of five appear), the concern-free Paper F tie-break is strictly suboptimal under registered concerns with exact rational gaps, the mirrored concern pair is reversal-natural, and the bag/pair_eq family has an exact phase boundary at epsilon = 11/27.

controls.description: Concern vectors are registered rational inputs; nothing is learned, sampled, or inferred.
cost(t|r) = n_fibres(r) if r represents t else 2*n_worlds, written before the run.
All expected costs, gaps, and the phase boundary are Fractions; no floats.
All mass on bag must reproduce the Paper F tie-break choice q_perm, anchoring the instrument to the banked baseline.
concern_does_work, concern_idle, and inconclusive are all valid passing runs.

gates.criterion: Cost rule, task family, concern set, and verdict rule specified before the run.
bag's representing set is all five menu screens, as banked in Paper F.
The full 5x6 screen-by-task cost matrix is recorded.
Exactly the six registered concern vectors are evaluated.
Gaps serialize as exact integers or fractions.
The mirrored concern pair chooses reversal-dual screens and the reversal is an involution on worlds.
The 55-point epsilon sweep matches the exact boundary 11/27 with the tie kept by fewest fibres.
Verdict is concern_does_work, concern_idle, or inconclusive.
No valence, agency, consciousness, learned concern, LLM, or master-object claim.
